new.s: How many seats were reserved for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures under the Poona Pact of 1932?
new.x: The Poona Pact raised the depressed classes' seats from 71 under the Communal Award to 148 reserved seats in joint electorates.
new.angle: U0391 notes gap: Poona Pact 148 seats

new.s: Which Act gave Muslims a separate electorate for the first time, introducing communalism into Indian politics under Lord Minto?
new.x: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) gave the first legal separate electorate for Muslims; hence Minto is called the father of the communal electorate.
new.angle: U0391 #4 Lord Minto -> measure and Act

new.s: Which pact, by which the Congress accepted separate electorates and weightage, is said to have legitimised communal politics?
new.x: The Lucknow Pact (1916) gave short-term Hindu-Muslim unity, but by accepting separate electorates it legitimised communal politics.
new.angle: U0391 notes gap: Lucknow Pact legitimised communal politics

new.s: With which leader is the All India Hindu Mahasabha, founded in 1915, associated?
new.x: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded in 1915 under the Maharaja of Kasim Bazar and is associated with Madan Mohan Malaviya.
new.angle: U0391 #4 founding of Hindu Mahasabha -> leader

new.s: In T.K. Oommen's classification, the Bahai community keeping away from politics is an example of which dimension of communalism?
new.x: Retreatist communalism is when a small community keeps away from politics, as the Bahai community does.

new.s: In T.K. Oommen's classification, the Gorkhaland demand is an example of which dimension of communalism?
new.x: Separatist communalism seeks a separate territorial state within India, such as Gorkhaland; secessionist seeks one outside India.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bipan Chandra gave three stages of communalism.
2. T.K. Oommen identified six dimensions of communalism.
3. W.C. Smith wrote 'Modern Islam in India'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: Bipan Chandra gave three stages, Oommen six dimensions, and W.C. Smith wrote 'Modern Islam in India'.

new.s: Who headed the commission set up by the Gujarat government to inquire into the Godhra train burning and the 2002 riots?
new.x: The Nanavati-Mehta Commission on Godhra and the 2002 Gujarat riots was headed by Justice G.T. Nanavati.
new.angle: U0392 PYQ y50469ca66c9 Inquiry commission -> head

new.s: Who headed the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities that reported in 2007?
new.x: Justice Ranganath Misra headed the NCRLM, which reported in 2007 on backward sections of religious and linguistic minorities.

new.s: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is outraging religious feelings (IPC Section 295A) now covered?
new.x: IPC 295A became BNS Section 299; IPC 153A became BNS 196 and IPC 505 became BNS 353.

new.s: In which State did the Muzaffarnagar communal riots of 2013 take place?
new.x: The Muzaffarnagar riots of 2013 took place in Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: Which body investigated the Godhra and 2002 Gujarat riot cases on the orders of the Supreme Court?
new.x: The Supreme Court appointed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the Godhra and Gujarat riot cases.

new.s: Under Article 16(3), which law did Parliament enact to lay down residence requirements for public employment?
o: Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957
AP Employment of Local Candidates in the Industries/Factories Act, 2019
new.x: Only Parliament can set residence rules under Article 16(3); it did so by the Public Employment (Requirement as to Residence) Act, 1957.

new.s: Who undertook a fast in 1951 for a separate Andhra State?
new.x: Swami Sitaram fasted in 1951 for Andhra State; Potti Sriramulu later became the first to fast unto death for it.
new.angle: U0393 notes gap: Andhra sequence -> Swami Sitaram's fast

new.s: What did the JVP Committee recommend in its report of April 1949?
o: It rejected the linguistic principle for the present, stressing unity and security
It recommended 'one language, one state' for all of India
It recommended 14 states and 6 Union Territories
new.x: The JVP Committee (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya) rejected the linguistic principle for the time being, stressing unity and security.

new.s:
Arrange the following States in the order of their formation in November 2000:
1. Uttarakhand
2. Jharkhand
3. Chhattisgarh
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Chhattisgarh was formed on 1 November, Uttarakhand on 9 November and Jharkhand on 15 November 2000.

new.s: Which was the first ethnic movement in India to win a State?
new.x: The Andhra Movement was the first ethnic movement to win a State, Andhra State in 1953.
new.angle: U0393 notes gap: first ethnic movement to win a State

new.s: Why did B.R. Ambedkar call India a 'Union of States'?
o: Because the States have no right to secede
Because the States were formed by an agreement among themselves
Because each State has its own Constitution
Because the States alone elect the President
new.x: Ambedkar explained that India is a Union of States because the States have no right to secede from it.
new.angle: U0393 notes gap: Union of States -> no right to secede

new.s: Which of the following Acts were withdrawn by the Andhra Pradesh Assembly in November 2021?
o: AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2020 and APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2020
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and Andhra State Act, 1953
AP Employment of Local Candidates in the Industries/Factories Act, 2019 and APCRDA Act, 2014
AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and APCRDA Act, 2014
new.x: In November 2021 a Repeal Bill withdrew both three-capitals Acts of 2020: the Decentralisation Act and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act.
new.angle: U0394 #1 Three capitals Acts -> repeal (PYQ y22a27479156 / y25bc185bb52 angle)

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the three-capitals legislation of Andhra Pradesh:
1. The APCRDA (Repeal) Act was passed in 2020.
2. The Repeal Bill withdrawing the three-capitals Acts was introduced in the AP Assembly in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The APCRDA (Repeal) Act came in 2020; the Repeal Bill withdrawing the three-capitals Acts was introduced in November 2021, not 2023.
new.angle: U0394 #1 Three capitals -> repeal date (PYQ y25bc185bb52 angle)

new.s: Under the 2020 three-capitals plan of Andhra Pradesh, which city was to be the legislative capital?
new.x: Amaravati was the legislative capital, Visakhapatnam the executive and Kurnool the judicial capital.

new.s: Which Articles were inserted in the Constitution by the 32nd Amendment, 1973, following the Six Point Formula?
new.x: The 32nd Amendment, 1973 inserted Article 371D (zonal system of local cadres) and Article 371E (central university in AP).
new.angle: U0394 #4 Six Point Formula -> Articles inserted

new.s: In which year was the Sri Bagh Pact between Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders signed?
new.x: The Sri Bagh Pact of 16 November 1937 was the first Coastal-Rayalaseema accord.

new.s: Which section of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 provides tax incentives to the residual State?
new.x: Section 94 of the AP Reorganisation Act provides tax incentives; Section 46(2)-(3) gives the backward-areas package.

new.s: Which Chief Minister of Gujarat resigned in February 1974 following the Nav Nirman movement?
new.x: The Nav Nirman student movement against corruption and prices forced Chief Minister Chimanbhai Patel to resign in February 1974.

new.s: Which was the first nationwide student mobilisation in India after Independence?
new.x: The JP movement of 1974, which began in Bihar, was the first nationwide post-Independence student mobilisation.

new.s: In which year did the AASU-led Assam Movement against illegal migrants begin?
new.x: The AASU movement ran from 1979 to 1985 and ended with the Assam Accord of 1985.
new.angle: U0395 PYQ y0311d6d479f Assam Movement -> start year

new.s: National Youth Day, observed since 1985, marks the birth anniversary of whom?
new.x: National Youth Day has been observed since 1985 on the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
new.angle: U0395 notes gap: National Youth Day -> Vivekananda

new.s: How many objectives does the National Youth Policy 2014 set out?
new.x: The National Youth Policy 2014 has 5 objectives and 11 priority areas.

new.s: Which movement of 2011 is regarded as the first major anti-corruption youth movement in India?
new.x: India Against Corruption (2011) was the first major anti-corruption youth movement.
new.angle: U0395 notes gap: India Against Corruption

new.s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2015, which was the leading cause of farmer suicides in India?
new.x: ADSI 2015 ranked bankruptcy or indebtedness first among causes of farmer suicides, followed by farming-related issues.

new.s: As per NCRB's ADSI 2015, which cause ranked second among causes of farmer suicides?
new.x: Farming-related issues came second after bankruptcy or indebtedness in ADSI 2015.

new.s: Which State tops the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment's state-wise list of beggars?
new.x: West Bengal has the highest number of beggars in the Ministry of Social Justice list.
new.angle: U0396 #2 State-wise beggar data -> top State

new.s: What did the Supreme Court decide in 2021 on a plea to ban begging?
o: It refused to ban begging, calling it a socio-economic problem
It banned begging in all public places
It upheld the punishment of beggars under the Bombay Act
It directed all States to arrest habitual beggars
new.x: In 2021 the Supreme Court refused to ban begging, saying it is a socio-economic problem.

new.s: In which year was the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment?
new.x: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan was launched on 15 August 2020 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
new.angle: U0396 #5 Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan -> year
